sbh2.4:1.2: In the three times, it is: mere formation, mere dharma, mere entity, mere cause, mere effect — consistent with reasoning, namely, by dependence-reasoning, by cause-and-effect reasoning,
sbh2.4:1.4: It is the bringing forth of dharmas by dharmas alone,
sbh2.4:1.5: and the absence of an agent or experiencer.
sbh2.4:2.1: Attending to this object, the person of delusion-conduct in whom delusion predominates abandons delusion,
sbh2.4:2.3: and purifies the mind from delusion-conduct.
